In 2008, the crisis was triggered by excessive leverage in subprime mortgage derivatives, causing major banks (like Lehman Brothers) to fail and credit markets to lock up. Today, corporate and bank balance sheets are well-capitalized, and global economic growth remains on solid footing. The current friction comes from sticky inflation (~3.7% in the US) and a valuation reset in mega-cap AI stocks—closer in character to the 2000 tech valuation reset or 1970s/2022 supply-driven inflation cycles than 2008.

In 2008, policymakers were terrified of a deflationary depression and were flooding the system with cheap money. Oil is priced around geopolitical risk premia in the Middle East rather than runaway speculative demand, and rising US/global output is keeping a lid on prices.

comments.text: Markets are always up & down. Some day green and some day red. Everyone talks about Portfolios but we are not billionaires invest and build Portfolios of 1-2 crores and wait for 5-10 years to see that Portfolios had grown to 30-50 %. Instead our main focus should be earnings either in the green market or in the red Market in PE & EC positions. Portfolios will sometimes be red and sometimes green. But the only thing we should remember and learn is to make money in this green and red bracket. Short positions in CE & PE we should buy and sell . We should not take the risk of thinking that it will go higher. Let's wait for more time. If you think in such a way then you are a loser. Make small profits and exit .
